claude.sample_unit: synthetic psychiatric intake vignettes per condition

links.outcome: Omission of embedded safety-critical risk fact in LLM psychiatric note summaries under generic prompt
links.effect: Baseline risk-fact omission ranged from 4% to 26% across four models; smallest model omitted the risk fact about one time in four; suicidality omitted up to 50% for weaker models.
links.quote: Baseline (generic-instruction) risk-fact omission ranges from 4% to 26% across the four models the smallest model omits the safety-critical fact roughly one time in four.

links.outcome: Risk-fact and routine-fact omission with versus without an added safety-priming prompt instruction
links.effect: Risk-fact omission fell 26%→8% (McNemar p = 0.016) for the worst model only; no reliable effect for the other three (p ≥0.62); routine-fact omission rose 6-20 points in three models.
links.quote: The safety-priming instruction produces a large, statistically signicant improvement for exactly the model with the worst baseline (26%→8%, paired McNemar p = 0.016) and no reliable eect for the other three (p ≥0.62).

unlisted_practices: Adding a safety-priming instruction to summarization prompts and validating it per model, given a trade-off of increased routine-fact omission
